## What the data says
- No PSI microgravity test runs exist for thin fabric at 30 % O₂, 70.3 kPa (zone **no_evidence**) [PSI-25][PSI-99].
- The predictor provides a physics estimate: with n-heptane surrogate the adiabatic flame temperature (~2550 K) is ~220 K above the hottest thin-fabric condition tested (≈2320 K) and ~530 K above the coldest burning condition (≈2010 K) [PSI-25][PSI-99].
- Droplet tests are the nearest evidence: 8 methanol droplet runs at 30-34 % O₂ and 71.2-72.1 kPa sustained burning; evidence coverage 0.892, physics margin ≈790 K [PSI-69].
- Fire-resistant materials (Nomex, silicone) were tested only up to 22.2 % O₂: 3 of 4 Nomex runs burned, 1 did not; 0 of 4 silicone runs burned [PSI-25][PSI-99].
- Outside PSI, Nomex HT90-40 failed NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 at 30 % O₂, 70.1 kPa in 1 g(NTRS 20070018178).
- Partial-gravity data are absent; NASA FM2 researchers note that flame-spread oxygen requirements may be lowest near lunar gravity, making partial gravity potentially more hazardous than both micro- and Earth-gravity(NTRS 20260000646).

## How confident we can be
- Evidence coverage for thin fabric is **none** at the target conditions; confidence relies solely on the physics estimate, not on test data.
- Solid-material data are dominated by "sustained" outcomes: 131 of 134 ordinary solid runs (PSI-25, PSI-98, PSI-99) sustained burning; only 2 extinction-velocity limits and 1 no-ignition run exist, preventing a flammability limit determination [PSI-25][PSI-98][PSI-99].
- Droplet evidence provides high coverage (0.892) for nearby oxygen/pressure, but applies to liquid fuels, not thin fabric.

## Gaps
- No thin-fabric test runs at 30 % O₂ and 70.3 kPa; the predictor's physics estimate lacks experimental validation.
- No solid-fabric data at pressures below 101.3 kPa; all solid runs are at ~101 kPa, limiting pressure extrapolation.
- No fire-resistant material data above 22.2 % O₂; behavior at lunar-base oxygen levels is untested.
- No partial-gravity combustion data; lunar-gravity effects remain unknown.

## What future experiments (e.g. LUCI, FM2) should measure
- Thin-fabric ignition, flame spread, and extinction at 30 % O₂ and ~70 kPa in partial gravity (≈0.166 g).
- Thin-fabric tests across a pressure range (50-100 kPa) to map pressure dependence.
- Fire-resistant material (Nomex, silicone) tests at 30 % O₂ and lunar-base pressure to verify performance beyond 22 % O₂.
- Droplet combustion of surrogate fuels on thin fabric substrates at target conditions to link liquid-fuel data to fabric behavior.
- Systematic partial-gravity runs to quantify any minimum oxygen requirement near lunar gravity.
